record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: Certain specific well-known (and lesser known) Banach algebras still need to be investigated in order to determine if they are, in fact, ordered Banach algebras and, if so, what properties their algebra cones possess. This list includes \(L^1(G)\) (with G a locally compact commutative group) and, in particular, \(L^1({\mathbb Z}) = \ell ^1\) (the Wiener algebra); the disc algebra both as an ordered subalgebra of the corresponding algebra of continuous functions and with the positive elements being the functions such that all coefficients in their Taylor series expansion are positive; the order bounded operators on a complex Banach lattice E (note that they are the same as the regular operators on E if E is Dedekind complete) and the multi-bounded operators on a complex Banach lattice.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a complex Banach algebra $A$ with unit is called an ordered Banach algebra if it contains a non-empty subset $C \subseteq A$, called the algebra cone, satisfying: (i) $C + C \subseteq C$, (ii) $\lambda C \subseteq C$ for all $\lambda \ge 0$, (iii) $C \cdot C \subseteq C$, (iv) $\mathbf{1}_A \in C$, and (v) $C \cap (-C) = \{0\}$. The cone $C$ induces a partial order on $A$ by $a \le b \iff b - a \in C$. Properties of interest for an algebra cone include being normal (there exists $\alpha > 0$ such that $0 \le a \le b$ implies $\|a\| \le \alpha \|b\|$), being closed, generating $A$ (i.e., $A = C - C$), and being proper.

Investigate the following Banach algebras and decide, in each case, whether the algebra is an ordered Banach algebra in a natural way, and if so, determine which of the above properties the natural algebra cone possesses:

(a) The group algebra $L^1(G)$ (with convolution product) for a locally compact abelian group $G$, and in particular the Wiener algebra $\ell^1(\mathbb{Z}) = L^1(\mathbb{Z})$.

(b) The disc algebra $A(\mathbb{D}) = \{f \in C(\overline{\mathbb{D}}) : f \text{ holomorphic on } \mathbb{D}\}$, considered with two candidate cones: 
 (b1) as an ordered subalgebra of $C(\overline{\mathbb{D}})$ with positive elements those $f \in A(\mathbb{D})$ taking nonnegative real values on $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$;
 (b2) with positive elements those $f \in A(\mathbb{D})$ whose Taylor coefficients at $0$ are all nonnegative real numbers.

(c) The algebra $L^b(E)$ of order bounded linear operators on a complex Banach lattice $E$ (which coincides with the algebra of regular operators when $E$ is Dedekind complete), and the algebra of multi-bounded operators on a complex Banach lattice $E$.

For each case, characterize the algebra cone and its order-theoretic and topological properties.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in a list of open problems on ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms. No comprehensive resolution covering all listed algebras (Wiener algebra, disc algebra in both orderings, order bounded operators, multi-bounded operators) appears in the literature; partial investigations exist for related order structures, but the problem as posed remains open.
